author: Latin Business Daily
title: Superintendence urges companies to report credit risk information as required by law
text:
Superintendence urges companies to report credit risk information as required by law
The Superintendence of Companies, Securities and Insurance reminded on July 22 companies under its supervision that engage in credit sales, direct financing, or any modality generating deferred payment obligations, as well as auxiliary service companies managing their own portfolios or acquiring them from public and private financial system entities, that they must directly and periodically report credit risk information to the Superintendence of Banks. This requirement is established under the Companies Law, the Regulation for Credit Sales Control and Card Issuance, and the Organic Monetary and Financial Code.
The Credit Data Registry System consolidates information about credit operations and payment obligations originating both in the financial system and other sectors of the economy. Its purpose is to analyze corresponding risks within a framework of transparency and reliability.
The Superintendence called on obligated entities to comply with this provision promptly and ensure that reported information is legal, truthful, complete, accurate, and current, in accordance with applicable regulations.
